allowed-roots.too-many_one: The app can have at most {{count, number}} media folder.
allowed-roots.too-many_other: The app can have at most {{count, number}} media folders.
allowed-roots.path-missing: Each media folder needs its path.
allowed-roots.too-long_one: A media folder's path can be at most {{count, number}} character long.
allowed-roots.too-long_other: A media folder's path can be at most {{count, number}} characters long.
allowed-roots.control-characters: A media folder's path can't contain line breaks or other control characters.
allowed-roots.not-full-path-windows: “{{path}}” is not a full path. Start it with a drive letter such as D:\.
allowed-roots.not-full-path-linux: “{{path}}” is not a full path. Start it with /.
allowed-roots.linux-path-on-windows: “{{path}}” is a Linux path, but this app runs on Windows. Give the folder's path inside the app, such as D:\Media.
allowed-roots.windows-path-on-linux: “{{path}}” is a Windows path, but this app runs on Linux. Give the folder's path inside the app, such as /media.
allowed-roots.whole-file-system-windows: “{{path}}” is the whole file system. Name the folder the media is in, such as D:\Media.
allowed-roots.whole-file-system-linux: “{{path}}” is the whole file system. Name the folder the media is in, such as /media.
allowed-roots.nested: “{{inner}}” is inside “{{outer}}”, which already allows it. Keep only “{{outer}}”.
allowed-roots.quarantine-holds-copies: “{{path}}” still holds replaced or removed copies, so its media folder can't be taken out of the list. Restore them or delete them permanently first.

replacement-folders.too-many_one: The app can have at most {{count, number}} library folder ticked for replacement.
replacement-folders.too-many_other: The app can have at most {{count, number}} library folders ticked for replacement.
replacement-folders.path-missing: Each library folder ticked for replacement needs its path.
replacement-folders.too-long_one: A library folder's path can be at most {{count, number}} character long.
replacement-folders.too-long_other: A library folder's path can be at most {{count, number}} characters long.
replacement-folders.control-characters: A library folder's path can't contain line breaks or other control characters.
replacement-folders.dot-segment: “{{path}}” contains . or .. as a folder name, so it can't be ticked for replacement.
replacement-folders.not-full-path: “{{path}}” is not a full path, so it can't be ticked for replacement.
replacement-folders.unknown-folder: “{{path}}” isn't a library folder the app knows, so it can't be ticked for replacement.

unreported.view-unknown: “{{value}}” is not a view of the files in no library. Use Problems, Extras or Ignored, or leave it out for every file.

inventory.no-allowed-roots: No media folder is allowed yet, so the app reads no file.
inventory.not-full-path: “{{path}}” is not a full path, so the app doesn't read it.
inventory.dot-segment: “{{path}}” contains . or .. as a folder name, so the app doesn't read it.
inventory.outside-allowed-roots: “{{path}}” is outside the media folders the app may read.
inventory.link-leads-out: “{{path}}” leads through a link to “{{target}}”, outside the media folders the app may read.
inventory.unfollowable-link: “{{path}}” leads through a link to “{{target}}”, which the app doesn't follow.
inventory.too-many-links_one: “{{path}}” leads through more than {{count, number}} link, likely a loop, so the app doesn't follow it.
inventory.too-many-links_other: “{{path}}” leads through more than {{count, number}} links, likely a loop, so the app doesn't follow them.
inventory.folder: “{{path}}” is a folder, not a file.
inventory.not-a-regular-file: “{{path}}” is not a regular file but a device, a socket or a pipe.
inventory.not-allowed-to-read: The app isn't allowed to read “{{path}}”.
inventory.time-out-of-range: The app couldn't read “{{path}}”: its modification time is outside the years 1 to 9999.
inventory.time-past-9999: The app couldn't read “{{path}}”: its modification time is past the year 9999.
inventory.changed-while-checking: “{{path}}” changed while the app was checking it: a folder on the way or the file itself became a link or something else, so the app didn't open it.
inventory.changed-while-reading: “{{path}}” changed while ffprobe was reading it, so what was read can't be said to belong to either version.
inventory.changed-while-hashing: “{{path}}” changed while the app was reading it for its hash, so the hash can't be said to belong to either version.
inventory.changed-while-hashing-pieces: “{{path}}” changed while the app was reading some of its pieces, so they can't be said to belong to either version.
inventory.media-unreadable: ffprobe couldn't read “{{path}}” as media: {{reason, message}}.
inventory.inspector-unavailable: The app couldn't start ffprobe ({{reason, vendor}}); the Docker image includes it, and elsewhere FFmpeg must be installed with ffprobe on the PATH.
inventory.empty-root: “{{path}}” is empty; if it is a mount, it may be away, so the files found in it before are kept.
inventory.unusable-name: A name in “{{folder}}” isn't valid text, so the app skips it.
inventory.path-too-long_one: “{{path}}” is longer than {{count, number}} character, so the app skips it and everything in it.
inventory.path-too-long_other: “{{path}}” is longer than {{count, number}} characters, so the app skips it and everything in it.
inventory.leads-back-up: “{{path}}” leads back to a folder above it, so the app doesn't walk it again.
inventory.limit-reached_one: The media folders hold more than {{count, number:grouped}} media file or {{folders, message}}, or links inside them lead to the same folders many times over, so the scan stopped.
inventory.limit-reached_other: The media folders hold more than {{count, number:grouped}} media files or {{folders, message}}, or links inside them lead to the same folders many times over, so the scan stopped.

ffprobe.not-a-container-clause: its content is “{{format, vendor}}”, which isn't a media container the app reads
ffprobe.timed-out-minutes-clause_one: it didn't finish within {{count, number}} minute
ffprobe.timed-out-minutes-clause_other: it didn't finish within {{count, number}} minutes
ffprobe.timed-out-seconds-clause_one: it didn't finish within {{count, number}} second
ffprobe.timed-out-seconds-clause_other: it didn't finish within {{count, number}} seconds
ffprobe.not-json-clause: its answer wasn't the JSON ffprobe writes

quarantine.not-linux: Only the app running on Linux renames or deletes a library file, as only there can a rename be made without ever replacing or copying one.
quarantine.not-in-quarantine: “{{path}}” isn't inside the quarantine at the top of a media folder.
quarantine.not-beside-quarantine: “{{path}}” isn't a file inside the media folder that holds the quarantine “{{quarantine}}”.
quarantine.folder-gone: The folder “{{folder}}” is gone, and the app creates no folder to put a file back.
quarantine.changed: “{{path}}” changed since the app checked it: its size, modification time, device or inode isn't what was read then.
quarantine.changed-while-checking: “{{path}}” changed while the app was checking it: a folder on the way or the file itself became a link or something else.
quarantine.no-identity: The file system holding “{{path}}” doesn't report a file's inode, so the app can't make sure it changes the file it checked.
quarantine.no-mount-id: This system doesn't say which mount “{{path}}” is on (Linux 5.8 or later does), so the app can't make sure a rename stays on one mount.
quarantine.other-mount: “{{path}}” and “{{other}}” are on different mounts, where a rename would be a copy.
quarantine.name-taken: “{{path}}” already holds a file, and the app never writes over one.
quarantine.not-allowed: The app's user isn't allowed to change “{{path}}”: renaming or deleting a file needs write and search permission on its folder, and on the one it goes into.
quarantine.rename-unsupported: The file system holding “{{path}}” can't rename a file without replacing a name already there, so the app renames nothing on it.
quarantine.swapped: What the app renamed from “{{from}}” to “{{to}}” isn't the file it checked: another file was put at that name just before the rename.
quarantine.could-not-change: The app couldn't rename or delete “{{path}}”: {{reason, vendor}}.

inspection.no-allowed-roots: No media folders are allowed yet. Add the folders the app may read under Media folders in the user menu, then inspect again.
inspection.queue-full: Too many file inspections are waiting. Try again in a minute.
inspection.restarted: The app restarted before this inspection finished. What it had read is kept.
inspection.app-error: The inspection stopped because of an error in the app. Its log says more.
inspection.no-allowed-roots-any-more: No media folders are allowed any more, so there was nothing to inspect. Add one under Media folders in the user menu.
inspection.identity-unknown: This platform gives files no identity (device and inode), so the app can't keep what it reads from them.
inspection.inspector-unavailable: The media inspector couldn't be started.
inspection.changed-while-reading: The file changed while it was being read; the next inspection reads it again.
inspection.media-unreadable: The media inspector couldn't read the file.
inspection.unreadable: The app couldn't read the file.
inspection.changed-since-look: A file changed after this inspection looked at it, so its hash counts from the next inspection.

scan.no-allowed-roots: No media folders are allowed yet. Add the folders the app may read under Media folders in the user menu, then scan again.
scan.queue-full: Too many folder scans are waiting. Try again in a minute.
scan.restarted: The app restarted before this scan finished, so nothing it found was stored. Scan the folders again.
scan.app-error: The scan stopped because of an error in the app. Its log says more.
scan.no-allowed-roots-any-more: No media folders are allowed any more, so there was nothing to scan. Add one under Media folders in the user menu.
scan.limit-reached: The scan reached its limit before it had walked every media folder, so it stopped.
scan.unscanned-place: The app didn't scan a place in the media folders.
